_README: Every declaration whose `#print axioms` line mentions Classical.choice, and
Coverage is by exhaustive sweep, not by the hand-written `#print axioms`
lines: audit.py generates a print for every declaration the parser can see.
Five Phase 1 results were classical and unaudited until it did -- a check that
only sees what someone remembered to print is not a check.
what justifies it. `tools/audit.py` fails if this file and the build disagree
in either direction, so a new classical result cannot land unexamined and a
stale entry cannot outlive its subject.
An audit line is an upper bound: it says a proof used choice, not that the
theorem needs it. The gap is visible in this tree: `cut_located`
and `located_bracket` are the same walk, and only one pays. So `reversed` is
the only status that establishes anything:
reversed   -- Reverse.lean proves, choice-free, that the statement implies
EM (or the weaker principle named). The dependency is real.
definition -- a def rather than a proposition; nothing to reverse.
inherited  -- classical only through something else it is stated over. Not
known to be essential; `note` says where the constructive
content lives.
open       -- classical, and no reversal found. Counted against
_open_budget, which ratchets: a new one fails the build, and
clearing one requires lowering the budget to lock it in.
There is no `accepted` status on purpose. If a result is genuinely classical
it can be reversed; if it cannot be, it is not yet understood -- and `open`
says exactly that instead of pretending otherwise.
axiom      -- a declared axiom of Phase 1. It is the subject of the audit,
not a result to be justified against it.
equivalent -- both directions: the statement implies the principle, and the
principle proves the statement, each choice-free. This pins the
result to exactly that strength, which a Phase 2 audit line
cannot do on its own -- Lean derives em from choice and reports
only choice.
`_equivalences` HOLDS REVERSALS, NOT TWO-WAY EQUIVALENCES, and the name
misleads. An entry records that its `statement` REVERSES to its
`principle` --- statement implies principle, witnessed by `reversal`. It
does NOT assert the converse. An entry may reverse to
a principle and say so in its own note; nothing claims
`llpo` gives back path selection.
SOME entries ARE two-way and say so in their note ---
A note may read "EQUIVALENT to em -- both directions
proved" --- but that is the note's claim, not the field's meaning.
MEASURED 2026-08-26, because the obvious check is wrong: of the ten
entries whose statement is also a lattice node, ONE is mutually reachable
in `lattice.json` and NINE are one-directional. A cross-registry check
asserting mutual reachability would report nine defects and be wrong about
all nine. This paragraph exists so that check does not get written --- the
registry was silent here, and a maintained registry is believed where it
says nothing.

_equivalences.note: deciding whether a walk-built real *is* zero. One quantifier weaker than membership in its cut, and correspondingly one step down the lattice from LPO
every subset of a finite set is finite. Both directions now: deciding how many elements {z in 1 | p} has decides p, and em supplies the detachability that isFinite_of_detachable needs

dne: reversed by `em_of_dne`. Pinned: Phase 1. Equivalent to em, not weaker
byContradiction: reversed by `em_of_byContradiction`. Pinned: Phase 1. dne under another name
byCases: reversed by `em_of_dne`. Pinned: Phase 1. Case analysis on an arbitrary proposition -- em applied
peirce: reversed by `em_of_peirce`. Pinned: Phase 1. Reverses with b := False
contrapose': reversed by `em_of_contrapose'`. Pinned: Phase 1. dne in disguise
not_and_or: reversed by `wem_of_not_and_or`. Pinned: Phase 1. De Morgan's third law -- weak excluded middle, not em. Same split as sdiff_inter one phase later
imp_iff_not_or: reversed by `em_of_imp_iff_not_or`. Pinned: Phase 1. Reverses at a := b
exists_not_of_not_forall: reversed by `wem_of_exists_not_of_not_forall`. Phase 1. Reverses to WEM, not em: the witness lands on Not a or on Not (Not a), and the second is where em would be needed. The earlier attempts failed because they aimed at em
drinker: reversed by `wem_of_drinker`. Phase 1. Same two-element family as exists_not_of_not_forall, same WEM
Exists.witness: reversed by `choice_of_witness`. Phase 1. Together with witness_spec it reconstructs the axiom, so it is choice rather than a consequence of it
Exists.witness_spec: reversed by `choice_of_witness`. Phase 1. The property half of the same reconstruction
em: Phase 1 declares it. The thing under audit, not a consequence of it
choice: Phase 1 declares it. Reconstructed by choice_of_witness, so Exists.witness is exactly this
decider_of_em: reversed by `em_of_decider`. Phase 1. The gap between proving by cases and defining by cases, measured: em is a hypothesis here, not an axiom, so [choice] is what turning Or p (Not p) into data costs. em_of_decider is the axiom-free converse. Phase 2's realMul, dcNum and dcDigit all sit on this

_families.name: the ternary walk
_families.carrier: a real named by a binary sequence, `nestLower (tlowSeq (boolDigit a))`
_families.varied: the LOGICAL FORM of the question
_families.result: four forms, four different lattice points -- lpo, wlpo, mp, llpo. Deciding a membership is Sigma and costs LPO; deciding an equality is Pi and costs WLPO; the implication between them is MP; the two-sequence form is LLPO.
_families.note: THE VARYING FAMILY. This is the only place the price moves while the object stays put.

_families.name: exact existence on the unit interval
_families.carrier: a uniformly continuous function on [0,1], located reals
_families.held_fixed: the logical form -- each is `exists c in [0,1]` with an EXACT condition at c
_families.varied: the mathematical content: maximum, mean value, zero crossing, intermediate derivative
_families.result: four contents, ONE lattice point -- llpo for all four.
_families.note: THE CONTROL, and the one that makes the ternary family mean something: it varies the other variable and the price does not move.

_families.name: selection from a binary tree
_families.held_fixed: carrier and form -- both produce a path from a non-emptiness
_families.varied: the hypothesis: not dying out, versus being infinite
_families.result: both llpo, and both converses open.
_families.note: A second control, weaker than the first because only two questions are asked.

_families.name: von Neumann ordinals
_families.varied: comparability of two, versus a least element of a set
_families.result: both em, both pinned in both directions.
_families.note: The third control, and the only family sitting at `em` rather than inside the omniscience lattice.
